title: Florida Senate, District 26
what_it_does: Represents District 26 in the Florida Senate; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: OPEN SEAT: Lori Berman (D) is term-limited (Ballotpedia). Ballotpedia snippets list Rep. David Silvers (D) in the Democratic primary and Rep. Rick Roth (R) in the Republican primary for SD 26; Yvette Drucker withdrew to run for Clerk (https://ballotpedia.org/Florida_State_Senate_District_26; https://floridapolitics.com/archives/760783-david-silvers-raises-56k-in-first-full-quarter-running-for-sd-26-quintupling-rick-roths-haul/). Primary results (and whether either faced a primary) could NOT be verified from snippets. Research limitation (Sept 2026): Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, dos.fl.gov, floridaelectionwatch.gov, Florida Politics and all news sites were blocked for fetching in this sandbox and the WebSearch budget was capped, so the roster is built only from search-result snippets; write-in/NPA qualifiers could not be checked. Positions are null because no snippet contained an explicit issue statement.

record.item: Voted against SB 300 (2023), the 2023 law limiting most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy.
Voted against HB 1 (2023), the 2023 law that made every Florida student eligible for a state-funded scholarship usable at private schools or for home education.
Voted against SB 254 (2023), the 2023 law barring gender-affirming medical treatment for minors and restricting it for adults.
Voted against SB 7050 (2023), the 2023 elections law that raised penalties and shortened deadlines for third-party voter-registration groups and changed vote-by-mail and voter-roll procedures.

Voted against SB 2-A (Dec. 2022), the December 2022 property-insurance law that ended one-way attorney fees and assignment of benefits and created a state reinsurance program, a market-based approach; a vote for it is coded as leaning against more direct state intervention.
Voted against HB 1 (2021), the 2021 Combating Public Disorder law that created new riot-related offenses and penalties and let the state override local cuts to police budgets.
Voted against HB 5 (2022), the 2022 law limiting most abortions to 15 weeks.
Voted against HB 1557 (2022), the 2022 Parental Rights in Education law restricting classroom instruction on sexual orientation and gender identity.
Voted against SB 90 (2021), the 2021 elections law that added identification requirements for mail-ballot requests and limited drop-box hours.

Voted against CS/CS/HB 1645 (2024), the 2024 energy law that removed climate change as a priority of state energy policy, repealed several renewable-energy goals and grant programs, banned offshore wind turbines in state waters and eased regulation of natural-gas pipelines; a vote for it is coded as leaning against promoting renewable energy.

Silvers sponsored a 2020 law establishing de-escalation protocols for Mobile Response Teams at schools, aimed at preventing unnecessary or traumatic Baker Act initiations for children, and bills requiring mental health facilities receiving minors under the Baker Act to begin a medical evaluation within 12 hours and allowing school districts to use mobile response units and crisis stabilization as a first line of help.

record.item: In 2024 Silvers worked on legislation establishing the Office of Children's Behavioral Health Ombudsman within the Department of Children and Families and requiring that parents be informed when minors are transported to behavioral health facilities. He also worked on changes to the Adult Protective Services Act requiring securities dealers and investment advisers to report abuse, neglect or exploitation of vulnerable adults, and sponsored legislation letting approved apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship programs count toward high school graduation requirements.

property_tax.summary: Roth said he favors Amendment 3, the November ballot measure raising the homestead exemption for non-school taxes, and that property tax relief is needed, while acknowledging it would hit poorer counties with lower property values hardest.
property_tax.quote: I just want a government we can afford. No one cuts payroll or taxes unless they are forced to.

insurance.summary: Mixed. Roth voted for SB 2-A in December 2022, the market-based property-insurance law that ended one-way attorney fees and assignment of benefits and created a state reinsurance program. His 2026 remedies pull both ways: he backs penalising insurers that fail to pay claims, which is stricter regulation, and separately legislation to encourage more competition in the industry to bring prices down, which is not.

other_issues.title: Says climate change is no longer a live issue in the U.S.
other_issues.summary: In the same September 2026 on-camera campaign interview, Roth said, 'Climate change is dead in America now,' and described the U.S. conflict with Iran as long-term oil policy. The quotes were published by Indivisible Boca Raton, a group supporting his opponent, alongside a link to the full interview.

other_issues.title: Data centers
other_issues.summary: Roth said he opposes data centers unless they provide some of their own power and water: 'I am totally against data centers until we figure it all out.'

other_issues.title: Immigration enforcement and farm labor
other_issues.summary: Roth said increased immigration enforcement has not affected his seasonal farm because it qualifies for H-2A workers, and that the H-2A program should be expanded to the nursery and landscape, dairy and beef cattle industries, which operate year-round and do not qualify. He said solutions can come from Congress once the illegal immigrant population returns to pre-2020 levels, and his advice to workers is 'If you like your job, keep your job. The state E-Verify requirement only applies to new hires.'
